---
title: "Pinning"
guide-section: "Core Workflows"
---

*Pinning* is recording the exact state of every object in a commit so it can
be read back later -- and, where the system supports it, holding that state
with a native reference that survives retention and cleanup. This page
assumes [Getting Started](01-getting-started.qmd) and moves to the objects a
lab actually has: an Icechunk repository on S3, a Neon Postgres database (an
experimental backend), and a directory of raw plate images on a shared
filesystem.

## Register the objects

```bash
tether init
tether add zarr/imaging --kind icechunk s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk --branch main
tether add db/metrics   --kind neon --project-id prj-9f2 --database metrics --role runner
tether add raw/plate1   --kind file /mnt/instruments/plate1/
tether status
```

```
dataset 0f2e9c7a11b3; on trunk bookmark main
       new  db/metrics  [neon/forkable]
       new  raw/plate1  [file/observed] unrecoverable
       new  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
```

`add` writes manifests only; `status` is the first command to contact the
systems. `--branch main` (the default) names the object's *upstream* branch,
the one the trunk bookmark stands for; `--at SNAPSHOT` starts from a chosen
state instead (see
[Starting from an older snapshot](04-branching-and-writing.qmd#starting-from-an-older-snapshot)).
The tiers say what pinning will mean for each object: Icechunk and Neon are
*Forkable*, so a native ref will be created; the directory is *Observed*, so
its state can be recorded but not re-read -- hence `unrecoverable`.

## Pin: the first commit

```bash
tether commit -m "Baseline: plate1 imaging + metrics"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
  pinned db/metrics -> tether.0a1b2c3d.a91f0e2b77c3e5f6
  recorded raw/plate1 (not recoverable)
committed 8d5719841a09
```

| Object | State recorded | Pin created |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zarr/imaging` | `snapshot_id` of `main` | Icechunk tag `tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6` (immutable; the default `expire_snapshots` keeps tagged snapshots) |
| `db/metrics` | `lsn`, `commit_xid` of `main` | Neon child branch `tether.0a1b2c3d.a91f0e2b77c3e5f6` at that LSN (protected only with `protected_pins = true`) |
| `raw/plate1` | `count`, `size`, `digest` | none; the per-file listing is stored under `.tether/listings/` |

Then the manifests (and the listing) were committed to your repository as
`8d5719841a09`:

```bash
jj diff -r 8d571984      # or: git show --stat 8d571984
```

```
Added regular file .tether/objects/zarr/imaging.toml:
        1: key = "zarr/imaging"
        2: kind = "icechunk"
        3: recoverable = true
        ...
       15: [state]
       16: snapshot_id = "K3F7Q2ZJ1XN4Y8W0"
       18: [pin]
       19: id = "0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6"
       20: ref = "tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6"
```

Pin ids are content-addressed from `(kind, locator identity, state)`. Commit
again without changing anything and every object is `unchanged`; no new refs
are created.

## Pin again after the data moves

Later, the imaging repository gets a new commit on `main` and the metrics
database has been written to. On the trunk those upstream branches *are* the
working refs, so a fan-out shows them modified:

```bash
tether status --snapshot       # fingerprint now; plain `status` shows the last snapshot
```

```
dataset 0f2e9c7a11b3; on trunk bookmark main
  modified  db/metrics  [neon/forkable]
     clean  raw/plate1  [file/observed] unrecoverable
  modified  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
```

`commit` pins the new heads (`tether pull` does the same and writes the
message for you):

```bash
tether commit -m "Re-segmented plate1; metrics through 2026-09-04"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.0a1b2c3d.deb4861eb388e5f6
  pinned db/metrics -> tether.0a1b2c3d.0c31e7aa5f92e5f6
committed cfc66fa79c0a
```

Two commits now describe two complete states of the whole dataset. Compare
them:

```bash
tether diff 8d571984 cfc66fa7 --content
```

```
    changed  db/metrics
    changed  zarr/imaging  [+0 -0 ~3 nodes]
               modified  /labels  12 chunks
               modified  /masks  12 chunks
               modified  /  group metadata
```

Neon has no native diff, so `db/metrics` shows only that it changed; Icechunk
reports the arrays whose chunks were rewritten.

## Reproduce reads from a pinned commit

This is the payoff. Any process can resolve every object *as it was* at a
commit:

```bash
tether open zarr/imaging -r 8d571984
tether open db/metrics -r 8d571984
```

```
s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk#tether.0a1b2c3d.6674305d5e1fe5f6
postgresql://runner@ep-quiet-lake-a1b2c3.us-west-2.aws.neon.tech/metrics?...
```

From Python the same handles come with native objects attached:

```python
from tether import Repo
from tether.handles import IcechunkHandle, NeonHandle

repo = Repo.find(".")

imaging = repo.open("zarr/imaging", rev="8d571984")
assert isinstance(imaging, IcechunkHandle) and imaging.read_only
store = imaging.session.store          # read-only icechunk session at the tag

metrics = repo.open("db/metrics", rev="8d571984")
assert isinstance(metrics, NeonHandle)
metrics.url                            # connection URL for the pinned branch
```

For reproducible jobs, set `TETHER_REV` instead of passing `rev` everywhere;
`repo.open(key)` then defaults to a read-only handle at that commit:

```bash
TETHER_REV=8d571984 python run_analysis.py
```

Record `TETHER_REV` (or `repo.vcs.current_rev()`) and each object's `pin.id`
next to your results and any output traces back to the exact state of every
input:

```python
provenance = {
    "tether_rev": os.environ.get("TETHER_REV") or repo.vcs.current_rev(),
    "pins": {k: (m.pin.id if m.pin else None) for k, m in repo.objects.items()},
}
```

`raw/plate1` cannot be opened at a revision: it is Observed, and its state at
`8d571984` is a digest, not an address. Directories that must be recoverable
belong in an object store with versioning enabled (single objects with
`--file versioned`).

## Drift

`status --snapshot` fingerprints everything, so drift surfaces the next time
you ask. The directory was registered with the default `--file immutable`, so
if a file under `/mnt/instruments/plate1/` changes -- its *content*; a `touch`
is not a change -- `status` stops:

```bash
tether status --snapshot
```

```
error: [raw/plate1] immutable object 'raw/plate1' changed since it was committed;
re-register with acceptance to record the new state
```

That is deliberate: an "immutable" input silently changing is the worst kind
of drift. Either the change is legitimate (`tether remove raw/plate1`, `add`
it again, commit) or something wrote where it should not have. Other objects
drift benignly: a branch that moved shows `modified` and is pinned by the next
commit; on the trunk, a branch-less object whose system moved past the pin
shows `behind` and waits for `pull`.

## Verify

Pins are references *inside other systems*, and those systems have their own
operators. `verify` confirms they still resolve to what the manifests say:

```bash
tether verify                      # working-tree manifests, cheap checks
tether verify -r 8d571984 --deep   # actually open each pinned state
tether verify --all-history --deep # every commit in the repository
```

```
        ok  8d5719841a09:db/metrics
        ok  8d5719841a09:zarr/imaging
        ok  cfc66fa79c0a:db/metrics
        ok  cfc66fa79c0a:zarr/imaging
```

A report is `ok`, `drifted` (the ref exists but points elsewhere), `missing`
(the ref or snapshot is gone), or `unknown` (cannot tell without `--deep`).
`--all-history` streams every manifest at every commit through one object
reader and verifies each distinct pin once, so it stays fast on long
histories. Exit status is 1 if anything is not `ok`, `unknown` included, so
the CI form is `verify --all-history --deep`: a Delta, DuckLake or
`--pin record` state can only be checked by opening it (see
[Sharing and CI](13-sharing-and-ci.qmd#a-ci-recipe)).

A pin is never taken on trust. Before `open --rev`, `new` from a commit, or
`promote --rev` reads or forks from one, the engine checks it against the
state the manifest recorded: a pin someone *deleted* falls back to the
recorded state where the backend can address it (the store usually still has
it -- `tether repair` recreates the ref); a pin someone *moved* is refused
with `PinDriftError`, because reading it would hand back the wrong data under
a commit's name.

## Garbage collection

Pins hold storage. When history no longer names a pin -- an aborted commit, a
squashed or abandoned commit -- `tether gc` releases it:

```bash
tether gc                 # dry run: print the plan
tether gc --no-dry-run    # release orphaned pins, prune unreferenced listings
```

Run `verify --all-history --deep` first; `gc` trusts history, and a pin that
is referenced but broken is a `verify` finding, not a `gc` one. Dropping
history on purpose, previewing store writes as plans, and cleaning up working
branches are covered in [Reclaiming Storage](05-reclaiming-storage.qmd).
